in_arabic.name: ديان
in_arabic.meaning: اسم الله الحسنى، الحاكم العادل القاضي بالعدل
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم من أسماء الله الحسنى، يعني الحاكم العادل الذي يقضي بالعدل بين عباده، وهو من الأسماء التي وردت في القرآن الكريم، مثل قوله تعالى: 'وَلِلَّهِ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى فَادْعُوهُ بِهَا' (الأعراف: 180)، ووردت أيضًا في السنة النبوية، مما يجعله من الأسماء ذات الأهمية الكبيرة في الإسلام.

in_urdu.name: دیان
in_urdu.meaning: اللہ کا نام، عادل حاکم، انصاف کرنے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: اللہ کے خوبصورت ناموں میں سے ایک، جس کا مطلب ہے عادل حاکم جو اپنے عباد کے درمیان انصاف کے ساتھ حكم کرتا ہے۔ یہ نام قرآن مجید میں وارد ہوا ہے جیسے کہ ارشاد ربانی ہے: 'وَلِلَّهِ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى فَادْعُوهُ بِهَا' (الاعراف: 180)۔ یہ نام مسلمانوں کے لئے بہت اہم سمجھا جاتا ہے کیونکہ یہ انصاف اور عدل کی تاکید کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: दियान
in_hindi.meaning: ईश्वर का नाम, न्याय करने वाला, इन्साफ़ करने वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: यह ईश्वर के सुंदर नामों में से एक है, जिसका अर्थ है न्याय करने वाला। यह नाम कुरआन में आया है, जैसे कि पवित्र कुरआन में कहा गया है: 'وَلِلَّهِ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى فَادْعُوهُ بِهَا' (अल-आराफ: 180)। यह नाम मुसलमानों के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण माना जाता है क्योंकि यह न्याय और इन्साफ पर जोर देता है।

in_pashto.name: دیان
in_pashto.meaning: د الله نوم، عادل حاکم، د انصاف کوونکی
in_pashto.long_meaning: د الله ښو نومونو څخه يو، چې معنی يې د عادل حاکم دی، چي د خپلو باندو په منځ کې يې د انصاف سره حکم کوي. دا نوم په قرآن کريم کې راغلی دی، لکه څنګه چې فرمايي: 'وَلِلَّهِ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى فَادْعُوهُ بِهَا' (الاعراف: 180). دا نوم د مسلمانانو لپاره ډير مهم دی ځکه چې دا د انصاف او عدل ټينګار کوي.

in_english.name: Dayyaanun
in_english.meaning: One of Allah's names, the just and fair ruler
in_english.long_meaning: Dayyaanun is one of the beautiful names of Allah, signifying the just and fair ruler. It is derived from the Arabic root 'D-Y-N' which means 'to judge' or 'to rule'. This name is mentioned in the Quran, such as in Surah Al-A'raf: 180, 'And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call Him by them.' It holds significant importance in Islam as it emphasizes justice and fairness. Muslims often choose this name to reflect the attributes of Allah.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dayyaanun (ديانون) holds significant cultural importance in Islamic societies. In the Arabic language, the term "dayyan" signifies someone who possesses extensive knowledge and experience, particularly within the context of Islamic law. This title is revered and respected within the legal system, where only qualified scholars are recognized as dayyans. The cultural weight given to the name can be attributed to the importance of knowledge and legal expertise in upholding justice and preserving the Islamic way of life.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Dayyaanun holds profound spiritual significance in Islamic tradition as well. It reflects the virtue of seeking knowledge, which is considered one of the key elements of faith. In the Quran, it is mentioned that Allah is the One who grants knowledge, and the Prophet Muhammad is often described as a source of knowledge for his followers. In the Sunnah, the Prophet emphasizes the importance of education, stating, "Seeking knowledge is an obligation for every Muslim." By carrying the name Dayyaanun, one is constantly reminded of the spiritual obligation to acquire wisdom and knowledge, and to utilize it for the betterment of others and the world around them.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidāyah wa'l-Nihāyah, vol. 12, pp. 134-135. The name Dayyaanun carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Describes Dhiyālah ibn 'Amr al-Kalbi, a poet from the Banu Bakr ibn Wa'il tribe who was also known as Dayyaanun due to his wisdom and knowledge. He is said to have composed poetry about the Battle of Hunayn in 630 CE in which Muhammad (pbuh) defeated the Meccan army.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hadī's Al-Futuḥāt al-Kubrā, vol. 2, p. 275. The name Dayyaanun carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mentions Al-Dayyaan ibn 'Abd al-Rahmān al-Khawlāni, a prominent scholar and judge during the caliphate of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Azeez (r. 717-720 CE). He was renowned for his knowledge, piety, and fair judgment.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Dayyaanun' in modern usage refers to an Islamic scholar or religious leader who provides guidance, counseling, and consultation on various aspects of Islamic law, ethics, and spirituality. This role is increasingly important in the context of a globalized world where Muslims are seeking to navigate their faith in diverse cultural and social contexts. Dayyaanun are sought after for their expertise in interpreting Islamic texts, applying Islamic law to contemporary issues, and providing guidance on ethical dilemmas. They can be found in various settings, including Muslim community centers, online Islamic forums, and Islamic educational institutions.
